subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Adjuvant endocrine and targeted therapy in early HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer

steps.tx: Hormone receptor positive early breast cancer means the tumour carries **oestrogen receptors**, so oestrogen fuels its growth. Adjuvant endocrine therapy forms the backbone of treatment and considerably cuts the risk of recurrence. The two main options are **tamoxifen**, which blocks the receptor, and **aromatase inhibitors** such as anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane, which reduce peripheral oestrogen production. The right choice depends on menopausal status and whether ovarian suppression is needed.

steps.tx: Aromatase inhibitors work only when ovarian oestrogen is suppressed, so in a **premenopausal** woman they must be paired with **ovarian function suppression**, usually a GnRH agonist such as goserelin. The SOFT and TEXT trials support this approach in high-risk premenopausal women. Tamoxifen alone is an alternative when AI use is not possible.

steps.tx: Aromatase inhibitor **arthralgia** is common and a leading reason for stopping. Management includes exercise, acupuncture and duloxetine, and if symptoms persist a switch to another AI or to **tamoxifen** keeps endocrine benefit. Bone density must be checked, since AIs cause accelerated bone loss, and **bisphosphonates** may be added in postmenopausal women.

steps.tx: Tamoxifen interacts with **CYP2D6**, which converts it into active endoxifen. Strong inhibitors such as paroxetine and fluoxetine reduce endoxifen levels, so venlafaxine or citalopram are preferred antidepressants. Extended therapy beyond 5 years, with an AI after tamoxifen, reduces late recurrence in higher-risk disease, though absolute gain is modest.

steps.tx: CDK4/6 inhibitors added to adjuvant endocrine therapy improve **invasive disease-free survival** in high-risk node-positive disease. Abemaciclib for 2 years is used in patients with 4 or more positive nodes, or 1 to 3 nodes with grade 3 or tumour 5 cm or more, based on the monarchE trial. Diarrhoea is the key toxicity: start loperamide early and hold the drug if it persists.
